evidence: OrderController.ts: place() uses parsePlaceOrderCommand(req.body) and list() uses parseOptionalState(req.query.state), so all input checks go through requestParsers.ts.

requestParsers.ts: parseOptionalState relies on the domain's isOrderState instead of keeping its own list of states; parseLine checks only that quantity is a number and leaves the business rule to the domain's InvalidQuantityError.
errorHandler.ts: statusFor is the only place that maps errors to status codes (NotFoundError→404, ValidationError→400, InsufficientStockError/InvalidOrderTransitionError→409, DomainError→422).
OrderController.ts: ADVANCE_ACTIONS only maps URL path segments to target states; whether a state change is allowed is still decided by advanceOrder.execute.
ProductController.ts: routes() exposes the single GET /stock endpoint, which calls ListProductStockUseCase. This is the same controller pattern as OrderController.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has one concern: it is the HTTP layer over the application use cases. The work is split cleanly across the files:
- The controllers (OrderController, ProductController) set up routes and pass calls to the use cases.
- requestParsers.ts holds all the checks that turn request input into use-case commands.
- errorHandler.ts is the only place that turns errors into HTTP status codes.

OrderController reads request input only through parsePlaceOrderCommand and parseOptionalState; it never checks req.body inline. ProductController has no input to parse. The parsers check only the shape of the request: type checks and non-empty strings and arrays. Business rules such as whether a quantity is valid or whether an order can move to a new state stay with the domain. The parser also uses the domain's isOrderState instead of keeping its own copy of the list of states.

ADVANCE_ACTIONS is only a table that maps URL path segments to target states. Which state changes are allowed is still decided by the AdvanceOrderUseCase and the domain. The error-to-status mapping appears only in statusFor. I found no rule or invariant written in more than one place, and no case where the module's own helpers are bypassed.
